1: Details & Features
The modular storage system is the ideal supplement for compressor units and ensures stable pressure supply for air and Nitrox applications. Available in pressure levels of 330, 350, and 420 bar, it minimizes pressure fluctuations during peak withdrawals and reduces the number of compressor start-ups.: Flexible expansion using 50- or 80-liter storage cylinders allows the system to be tailored precisely to individual demand, supporting smooth and efficient operation.
Storage cylinder with console: A module consists of a storage cylinder that is pre-piped and ready for connection, mounted on a console for floor or wall installation. Based on 50 l or 80 l storage cylinders, these storage systems can be expanded as required.
Pressure vessel: The storage cylinders comply with DGRL2014/68/EU (PED) and are intended for stationary applications.
Condensate drain: Depending on the application or due to insufficient air or gas treatment, condensate can accumulate in high-pressure storage systems. All standard storage vessels from BAUER KOMPRESSOREN are therefore equipped with a manual condensate drain.
Options: Safety valve and pressure gauge
Safety valve and pressure gauge are mounted on the console of the first module. This is mandatory if exceeding the maximum permissible storage pressure cannot be otherwise avoided, e.g. by approved safety valves on the compressor or in the pipeline.: The storage design
Storage system design – the basis for efficient compressor operation: A correctly dimensioned storage system is one of the key components of a high-pressure setup. It reduces pressure fluctuations during intermittent air withdrawal and decreases compressor start frequency by providing sufficient storage capacity. The pressure vessels and final separators in high-pressure compressors are designed for a limited number of load cycles. Fewer start-stop cycles significantly extend the service life of these components.
To ensure optimal operation, the compressor should ideally run no more than two to four cycles per hour. BAUER industrial compressors are equipped with cycle counters as standard, which record actual start cycles and support safe, efficient system control.: The size of the storage system depends on:
Compressor delivery rate (l/min): Air consumption of the specific application
Pressure differential between start and stop (hysteresis): Simplified formula for sizing a high-pressure storage system (based on 4 load cycles/hour):
Vk (l/min): Compressor delivery volume in liters per minute: V (l): Storage volume in liters (water volume)

What
is the I26 series used for?
The I26 series comprises water-cooled high-pressure compressors for the compression of air and nitrogen. It is used whenever these gases need to be reliably compressed from atmospheric pressure to high final pressures and supplied over long periods in continuous operation. Typical applications include industrial compressed air and nitrogen supply, process gas systems, research and development, test facilities and applications with permanent high-pressure demand where thermal stability and high operational reliability are required.
What
performance ranges does the I26 series cover?
The I26 high-pressure compressors achieve final pressures from 90 to 420 bar. The effective delivery rates range from approximately 2,200 to 3,300 litres per minute, depending on configuration, inlet pressure and operating conditions. This makes the series suitable for medium to high-capacity industrial applications in continuous operation.

results.content:
Document: GIB 23 series · Water-cooled boosters | BAUER KOMPRESSOREN
existing inlet pressure and increases it to the required final pressure. In contrast, a compressor compresses gas directly from atmospheric inlet pressure.
What
pressure ranges does the GIB 23 series cover?
Depending on the configuration and available inlet pressure, GIB 23 high-pressure booster compressors achieve final pressures of approximately 90 to 420 bar.
What
flow rates do the GIB 23 boosters provide?
The GIB 23 series covers flow rates of approximately 1,450 to 3,900 litres per minute. The actual flow rate depends on the inlet pressure, final pressure and system configuration.
Which
gases can be compressed with GIB 23 boosters?
GIB 23 boosters are designed for the compression of Air, Nitrogen, Helium, Heliox and Argon. They are specifically developed for industrial applications with increased pressure requirements.
How
are GIB 23 boosters controlled and monitored?
The boosters are equipped with the B-CONTROL MICRO control system. It enables easy operation, reliable monitoring of all relevant operating parameters and connection to the B-CLOUD and the B-APP for digital system monitoring.
What
advantages does the B-CLOUD offer for GIB 23 booster applications?
The B-CLOUD enables digital remote monitoring of the booster system. Operating data, alarms and system statuses can be accessed in real time, supporting predictive maintenance and high system availability.

A correctly dimensioned storage system is one of the key components of a high-pressure setup. It reduces pressure fluctuations during intermittent air withdrawal and decreases compressor start frequency by providing sufficient storage capacity. The pressure vessels and final separators in high-pressure compressors are designed for a limited number of load cycles. Fewer start-stop cycles significantly extend the service life of these components.

Air consumption of the specific application

We recommend a pressure differential Δp of max. 60 bar for continuous operation. Within this range, stationary high-pressure storage cylinders are typically rated for continuous duty. For higher differentials, the number of allowable filling cycles is limited. Please refer to the documentation for the specific pressure vessel.

Storage system design – the basis for efficient compressor operation

To ensure optimal operation, the compressor should ideally run no more than two to four cycles per hour. BAUER industrial compressors are equipped with cycle counters as standard, which record actual start cycles and support safe, efficient system control.

What
is the I26 series used for?
The I26 series comprises water-cooled high-pressure compressors for the compression of air and nitrogen. It is used whenever these gases need to be reliably compressed from atmospheric pressure to high final pressures and supplied over long periods in continuous operation. Typical applications include industrial compressed air and nitrogen supply, process gas systems, research and development, test facilities and applications with permanent high-pressure demand where thermal stability and high operational reliability are required.
What
performance ranges does the I26 series cover?
The I26 high-pressure compressors achieve final pressures from 90 to 420 bar. The effective delivery rates range from approximately 2,200 to 3,300 litres per minute, depending on configuration, inlet pressure and operating conditions. This makes the series suitable for medium to high-capacity industrial applications in continuous operation.

What
pressure ranges does the GIB 23 series cover?
Depending on the configuration and available inlet pressure, GIB 23 high-pressure booster compressors achieve final pressures of approximately 90 to 420 bar.
What
flow rates do the GIB 23 boosters provide?
The GIB 23 series covers flow rates of approximately 1,450 to 3,900 litres per minute. The actual flow rate depends on the inlet pressure, final pressure and system configuration.
Which
gases can be compressed with GIB 23 boosters?
GIB 23 boosters are designed for the compression of Air, Nitrogen, Helium, Heliox and Argon. They are specifically developed for industrial applications with increased pressure requirements.
How
are GIB 23 boosters controlled and monitored?
The boosters are equipped with the B-CONTROL MICRO control system. It enables easy operation, reliable monitoring of all relevant operating parameters and connection to the B-CLOUD and the B-APP for digital system monitoring.
What
advantages does the B-CLOUD offer for GIB 23 booster applications?
The B-CLOUD enables digital remote monitoring of the booster system. Operating data, alarms and system statuses can be accessed in real time, supporting predictive maintenance and high system availability.
